claim_evidence.claim_text: The pinned repository exposes several ingress surfaces over a shared `AIAgent` runtime. This case traces the classic `hermes chat` path from `hermes_cli.main.cmd_chat` through `cli.HermesCLI`, `AIAgent.run_conversation`, `agent.conversation_loop.run_conversation`, tool execution, turn finalization, and session persistence.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Boundary and representative configuration
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the pinned classic CLI path; alternate ingresses received targeted or survey treatment

claim_evidence.claim_text: Lifecycle is nested rather than singular: process and CLI session own a sequence of user turns; each turn owns model iterations and tool calls; compression, delegated children, persistent goals, background reviews, gateway sessions, cron jobs, and batch samples introduce additional boundaries with different persistence and completion semantics. The plugin hook named `on_session_end` fires after every `run_conversation` turn, whereas memory-provider and context-engine shutdown occur at actual session boundaries.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: One turn, end to end; Taxonomy friction
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the named boundaries; not every ingress was traced end to end

claim_evidence.claim_text: Hermes constructs and caches a system prompt from identity, task guidance, project instructions, a filtered skill index, memory/profile snapshots, environment, and provider/model metadata. Each call then adds the current history projection, ephemeral plugin and external-memory context, tool schemas, prefill, and provider-specific normalization.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: The system prompt is a session snapshot; the request is a turn projection
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the pinned path; exact prompts remain configuration, provider, plugin, project, and session dependent

claim_evidence.claim_text: Memory, profile, date, and related material labeled volatile during prompt construction normally become session snapshots because the complete system prompt is cached until explicit invalidation or compression rebuilds it. Mid-session durable writes do not automatically refresh the already cached prompt.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: The system prompt is a session snapshot; the request is a turn projection
claim_evidence.confidence: moderate-high for the inspected cache path; plugins or alternate context engines may refresh differently

claim_evidence.claim_text: The normal loop is model-directed over tool calls and text completion inside a programmed envelope that owns iteration budgets, interrupts, provider restoration/fallback, retries, context-pressure compression, malformed-output recovery, tool-name and argument validation, persistence ordering, verification nudges, and finalization. Known-truncated tool arguments fail closed without execution.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: A model-directed loop inside a recovery envelope
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the inspected loop; runtime integrity does not establish semantic task success

claim_evidence.claim_text: Tool mediation has distinct authority and observation stages: visible schemas come from filtered runtime definitions; middleware, plugins, approvals, guardrails, and optional checkpoints can alter or block a request; execution returns a raw result; post-processing can add guardrail guidance, transform or spill large results, add retrieval hints, normalize multimodal content, and only then append the model-facing tool observation.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Action authority and model-visible evidence are different stages
claim_evidence.confidence: high for built-in and registry dispatch paths; installed extensions can change semantics

claim_evidence.claim_text: SQLite is the canonical session/message store on the traced path. Inbound user content is persisted before the model call, assistant tool calls are persisted before tool side effects, and results are persisted after execution. Fresh built-in configuration enables in-place compression: old rows are soft-archived while a summarized active projection is inserted under the same session ID; legacy rotation remains supported.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Durable history is not active context
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the pinned fresh-default path; user configuration and upgraded installations may differ

claim_evidence.claim_text: Built-in context compression uses a lossy active projection with protected head and recent tail, tool-output pruning, and an LLM-produced structured summary. Depending on error class and configuration, summary failure can abort or use a deterministic placeholder while dropping middle turns; repeated compression is explicitly warned as quality-degrading.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Durable history is not active context
claim_evidence.confidence: high for mechanics; semantic retention and task impact were not behaviorally evaluated

claim_evidence.claim_text: Built-in durable memory is bounded `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` state, enabled by fresh defaults with writes not approval-gated. At most one optional external memory provider can add retrieval and asynchronous turn synchronization; committed built-in writes can be mirrored, while staged or failed writes are excluded.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Memory is bounded state, retrieval, and later adaptation—not one feature
claim_evidence.confidence: high for built-in and provider-manager boundaries; external-provider internals and memory quality remain outside the case

claim_evidence.claim_text: Top-level model delegation is forced into asynchronous background execution, while orchestrator-child delegation is synchronous. Children receive fresh budgets and sessions, inherit no broader capability than the parent, can use configured model/provider overrides, and return bounded summaries; fresh defaults allow three concurrent children, depth one, 50 iterations, no wall-clock timeout, and noninteractive denial of dangerous-command approvals.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Delegation changes scheduling and context, not epistemic independence
claim_evidence.confidence: high for orchestration mechanics; no causal quality or cost-benefit study was run

claim_evidence.claim_text: Ordinary text completion can stop the main loop without a general independent task judge. A separate verification-on-stop policy can suppress premature completion after code-like edits when fresh passing execution evidence is absent and ask the same agent for bounded follow-up verification. A missing config file is treated as current and inherits surface-aware `auto`; an existing versionless file is treated as legacy, and an unset or `auto` value is written as `false` when migration runs, as it is for affected older versioned installations. Thus “the default” depends on configuration origin and migration history.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Hermes has three different verification layers
claim_evidence.confidence: high for policy and configuration-generation behavior; the nudge does not execute tests or independently judge arbitrary tasks

claim_evidence.claim_text: Optional persistent `/goal` mode wraps ordinary turns in an auxiliary judge loop that can use structured verification criteria, user-added subgoals, and live background-process state. A done verdict stops; continue re-enters the same session; wait parks the loop; API failures continue fail-open; repeated parse failures and the 20-turn fresh default pause rather than loop indefinitely.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Hermes has three different verification layers
claim_evidence.confidence: high for optional mechanics; judge reliability and task benefit are unmeasured

claim_evidence.claim_text: Plugins and middleware are cross-cutting injection surfaces rather than a single subsystem: they can observe or change model requests, ephemeral context, tool requests, approvals, execution, tool results, verification, sessions, subagents, and gateway events. Some security-sensitive approval paths fail closed, while many observation/transformation hook failures are isolated or fail open to preserve availability.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Extensions cross every responsibility
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the hook vocabulary and inspected call sites; third-party behavior remains unknowable

claim_evidence.claim_text: Hermes performs periodic across-run adaptation: every ten eligible turns or tool iterations, a best-effort background fork can update durable memory or skills using conversation content, corrections, preferences, and observed techniques. The fork is isolated from canonical session persistence and external memory providers, restricted to memory/skill tools, and uses the main model by default; successful writes can apply without human approval under fresh defaults.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: The self-improvement loop adapts artifacts without an outcome objective
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the mechanism and defaults; learned-artifact correctness and downstream outcome impact are not established

claim_evidence.claim_text: The enabled-by-default curator normally performs deterministic usage/recency maintenance and recoverable archival; LLM consolidation is disabled by default. `/learn` is an ordinary prompted agent turn that asks the model to research and create one skill, and the learning graph visualizes stored artifacts, usage metadata, and lexical overlap. None is a measured outcome-optimization loop.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: The self-improvement loop adapts artifacts without an outcome objective
claim_evidence.confidence: high for observed mechanisms and moderate-high for bounded absence of an outcome objective in these paths

claim_evidence.claim_text: The pinned implementation records session messages, tool traces, token and cost usage, model/provider state, activity, and optional plugin telemetry; batch mode can record trajectories. These observability surfaces do not by themselves score task success or feed outcomes back into automatic policy optimization.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Observability can support evaluation without being evaluation
claim_evidence.confidence: high for present mechanisms and bounded negative claim; private evaluation systems remain unknown

claim_evidence.claim_text: Hermes and the reviewed OpenClaw repository have distinct recorded Git roots. Hermes later added an explicit OpenClaw migration, an OpenClaw-inspired permissions change, an OpenClaw-modeled subagent prompt, and a named port of an OpenClaw streaming fix. This establishes migration compatibility and selective mechanism-level influence, not whole-repository fork descent or independent convergence.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: OpenClaw relationship: translation and selective borrowing
claim_evidence.confidence: high for named evidence and low for any broader ancestry inference

claim_evidence.claim_text: Reachable code, comments, tests, and selected history show substantial engineering devoted to runtime and recovery invariants—prompt/session isolation, persistence-before-effects, malformed-call handling, compaction, delegated-child bounds, and background-review containment—while task acceptance remains narrower and surface-dependent. The evidence identifies concrete failure surfaces, not their frequency or relative cost.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: The self-improvement loop adapts artifacts without an outcome objective; Negative findings and what remains unknowable
claim_evidence.confidence: moderate-high for the allocation inference; no incidence, effort accounting, or outcome experiment was performed

claim_evidence.claim_text: External evidence qualifies rather than validates Hermes's mechanisms: recent compaction preprints report loss, variance, and latency under other protocols; BenchAgent reports that multi-agent workflows can underperform a matched single-agent anchor; MemoryAgentBench separates memory competencies and finds no evaluated method masters all; self-correction reviews favor reliable external feedback; production evaluation guidance separates trajectories from outcomes.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Research evidence: qualification rather than validation
claim_evidence.confidence: moderate-low to moderate transfer confidence; none directly evaluates Hermes v0.18.2

claim_evidence.claim_text: Hermes observes TF-001 through TF-007 and adds two candidate cross-cutting questions: configuration origin and generation can make no-file fresh, versionless existing, versioned migrated, explicitly configured, and runtime-effective values diverge; lineage can vary by mechanism inside one system relationship. These are Checkpoint 3 inputs, not approved taxonomy changes.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Taxonomy friction
claim_evidence.confidence: moderate for Hermes observations and low-to-moderate for general taxonomy implications until four-case consolidation

claim_evidence.claim_text: The concurrent registry-tool path may traverse execution middleware at both the agent wrapper and registry dispatcher, while the sequential path appears to traverse only the inner wrapper. Static inspection did not establish whether middleware actually executes twice, and no authorized behavioral check was run.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Action authority and model-visible evidence are different stages
claim_evidence.confidence: low; treat as a focused test candidate, not a defect or frequency claim

claim_evidence.claim_text: Fresh configuration selects the local terminal backend. Foreground commands execute through a `LocalEnvironment` that spawns shell processes directly on the host, and local background commands use the host process registry; Docker, Singularity, Modal, Daytona, and SSH are configurable alternatives. Approvals, guardrails, safe mode, working-directory validation, and credential filtering are policy or exposure controls, not host-process isolation.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Action authority and model-visible evidence are different stages
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the fresh default and built-in dispatch paths; configuration can select isolated or remote backends and no behavioral containment test was run

claim_evidence.claim_text: Explicit OpenClaw migration can reduce operator conversion work, but it does not establish semantic equivalence where mapped concepts have different lifecycle, context, authorization, or persistence contracts. Unsupported concepts are archived for manual handling.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: OpenClaw relationship: translation and selective borrowing
claim_evidence.confidence: moderate for the transfer-risk inference; no migration-success, semantic-equivalence, switching-cost, or outcome study was inspected

claim_evidence.claim_text: The classic CLI lazily resolves model, provider, API mode, credentials, and an eligible provider-scoped credential pool per turn, rebuilding the agent when the route signature changes. Recovery can rotate credentials within one provider or activate an ordered cross-provider/model fallback; each later turn normally attempts to restore the primary runtime unless cooldown remains active. Request fields are rebuilt for the active transport on each attempt.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: One turn, end to end
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the classic CLI and shared AIAgent route; deployment configuration and adapter-specific behavior can differ
